item.title: Hopefully, they will show all the good things
item.description: The President will be on “60 Minutes” tonight, and hopes the programme will show everything good done in two years, and asks the Republican Senate for help.

item.title: Send them directly to me
item.description: Threats against Republican donors are illegal, the President says: report them to the Department of Justice, or directly to him. A real president, and six regions, reply.

item.title: A Press Secretary like none other
item.description: The head of the UFC is offered the White House podium, with champion fighters as assistants, to defend the administration against the Lunatic Left.

item.title: Extortion at the highest level
item.description: Democrats are threatening officials with impeachment and donors with prison, without reason, the President says; he orders the Department of Justice to look into it.

item.title: A new Chief of Staff
item.description: Stephen Miller becomes Chief of Staff on Monday; Susie Wiles moves to the political operation, with thanks.

item.title: Nobody wants to say that
item.description: Without him, the President writes, Israel and the entire Middle East would not exist today. Nobody wants to say it; everybody knows it.

item.title: Joe will never let you down
item.description: A Complete and Total Endorsement for the RNC Chairman, who once named the President Statesman of the Year. Twice.

item.title: Super Intelligence is GOLD
item.description: The President is 100% in favour of Super Intelligence, and of the states that get rich from it; those that say no are foolish. Twenty-two regions and four statesmen reply.

item.title: Newsmax says so
item.description: Early morning: the President shares a headline that calls him a winner. A real president would have let it go.

item.title: We would have won in a landslide
item.description: On the evening of the midterm elections, the President points out that he was not on the ballot, and says that if he had been, he would have won in a landslide.
